verdict.rationale: Convex documents schema pushes to an isolated dev deployment, local deployments for development, and preview deployments as a plan feature. Its official MCP server lets agents work with deployments and is blocked from production by default, so an agent can iterate on schema changes outside production. However, preview deployments appear only as a pricing-page line, and nothing documents an agent-driven flow for creating a branch or preview environment, testing schema migrations there, and promoting them to production. Missing for 10: documentation of preview/branch deployment creation and lifecycle, documented schema-migration testing and promotion from preview to production, agent-driven preview workflow, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can let an agent create and test schema changes in an isolated branch or preview environment before production

citations.quote: When you change a function or the schema, the new versions are pushed to your dev deployment and the generated types in convex/_generated are updated.
It's also possible to run a Convex deployment locally for development.
The Convex Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides several tools that allow AI agents to interact with your Convex deployment.
By default, the MCP server cannot access production deployments. This is a safety measure to prevent accidental modifications to production data.
